body:
Renewed assessment for the user-requested recovery and inclusive-limit clarification: independently compared the complete current plan with its preceding approved subject and unchanged approved three-model package. The new wording uses the actual recorded recovery basis rather than current-manifest presence or an unrelated transport version. Source loadJournal selects V1_FORMAT for journal.version1 and V2_FORMAT for2; the writer persists version:this.format.version. Therefore the earlier draft's independent-bookkeeping-schema1 phrase is not a supported journal format. The plan correctly introduces no such format: positive recovery uses existing version2 and consistent saved manifests/writes/read set, including absent-current-manifest initial creation; schema1 remains the advanced RESULT envelope. Retired/unknown/inconsistent/ambiguous basis and unknown target bytes stop before restore/complete effects with recovery evidence preserved. Existing committed-state and identity rules are expressly retained. This resolves the substantive protection concern without accepting a contradicted version premise or expanding Design.

TG-03 now explicitly allocates below/exactly-at/over boundaries for 1,024 directories, 64 candidates and 8 MiB. Exactly the maximum is permitted when all other validity/size requirements hold; 65 candidates exceeds64. This matches CLI's exceeding-a-bound condition rather than changing it, and protects against an off-by-one implementation. M2 owns direct public/complete-module proof; TG-FINAL-01 repeats the supported recovery/absent-manifest integration after the full change. No new journal schema, storage guarantee or milestone boundary is introduced.

The fresh plan-recovery-and-limit-clarification evidence is authoring/source-check evidence only (readability89 warnings and whitespace pass), not a runtime recovery or limit test result. Current primary context, subject inspection and complete plan coherence were reassessed before renewing applicability. No material finding emerged; all retained four-milestone trace, source boundaries, proof timing, scoped test de-contracting and final-review/Verify dependencies remain adequate.

Scope: independent formal/manual Delivery Review of the complete exact primary plan, stable package member primary-plan at docs/plans/2026-09-08-retire-legacy-record-formats.md. The current approved design-review covers Record Format, CLI and Workflow; its three first-pass findings are explicitly resolved with retained origins. Proposal and Design scope remain unchanged. Navigation docs/plan.md is an index, not package state or an additional primary member. No plan, model, implementation, work initialization or routing edit was made by this reviewer.

Traceability: all RF-SR-01–08, CLI-SR-01–23 and WF-SR-01–17 are allocated to milestones and TG groups. The requirement table, eight-dimension allocation and group cases jointly identify the architecture boundary, responsible implementation slice, required observation and concrete command/manual evidence. The scoped R14/R17–20/R22–25 Design decisions are allocated to current evidence/dispositions and M4 consumer amendments. RC/Test remain policy dependencies; this plan neither grants their authority to a CLI check nor changes stored fields/transport versions.

Safe sequence: M1 separates neutral transport/path/configuration dependencies while existing acceptance remains unchanged, with before/after and full affected-module proof. M2 cuts stored-v1 recording/recovery acceptance and moves workflow-context to the exact v2 structural classifier after dependencies are separate; directly affected caller/selector changes are simultaneous. M3 removes remaining compact/lifecycle/new-change dispatch, exclusive engines, schemas, activation and test support after current discovery no longer depends on them. M4 completes governance, transitive skill resources and generated packages. Every dependent milestone waits for independent review and required corrections. Intermediate support/guidance states are explicitly development-only; release/customer adoption cannot occur on a partial milestone. Each rollback unit includes its coupled tests/consumers and does not rewrite v2 or archival data.

Source feasibility: inspected actual record-store format/journal and CLI dispatch boundaries, schema bundler, workflow-context and Python metadata/query/automation/selector imports. The schema bundler currently copies stored-v1 alongside transports, so M1 extraction and M2 generator reconciliation are necessary and allocated. workflow-context and Python helpers currently depend on legacy parsers/state, making their neutral-helper extraction and direct caller closure substantive. The plan covers those source families and demands exact existing/new/deleted path and caller dispositions before each milestone edit. Responsibility-bounded discovery may expand implementation paths but cannot silently change behavior, unrelated scope or milestone boundaries; those require reviewed replanning/Design. This gives execution a bounded inventory without pretending every transitive path is already known.

Test retirement: the nine current compact test modules exist, while record-store modules mix legacy stored acceptance, retained schema1 transports and v2 protection. M2/M3 distinguish actual cases and partitions rather than deleting by name. Dedicated acceptance leaves with explicitly retired capability; shared safety, independent-version tests, current rejection and useful diagnostics remain in existing harnesses. The already deleted thirteen suites are not removed again or recreated wholesale, and their lost coverage is not misrepresented as this retirement proof. Unknown protection requires bounded disposition; unavailable prior execution stays explicit. Full surrounding modules run after relevant fixture/helper edits and before milestone closeout; pre-change or focused-only passes cannot satisfy that obligation.

Proof adequacy: TG-01 preserves extracted semantics and unknown-vocabulary rejection. TG-02 covers real primary/advanced publisher paths, immutable origin and references, same-batch targets, exact neighbor bytes, conflicts/mixed writers, lost-response retries, bounded diagnostics, correction after completion and version2 prepared/committed initial/update recovery. Version1/unknown/mismatched/third-state journal stops have explicit no-mutation proof. TG-03 covers every classifier row/precedence, malformed v2 versus YAML archives/residue, unsafe enumeration, explicit-ID isolation, limits, schema2 scope/selection and configuration override rejection. TG-04/05 prove removed public and helper/validator paths unavailable before effects, no legacy automation fallback, unchanged archive bytes and no dangling imports/selectors. TG-06 checks current governing consumers, complete transitive public resources, portability and actual generated archive/metadata parity. These are meaningful outcome boundaries; keyword matching alone cannot prove them.

TG-FINAL-01 allocates fresh integrated public scenarios over an isolated mixed v2/archive project plus package/source/record identities. It composes extraction, format rejection, discovery, correction, origin, concurrency and recovery with current installed guidance. Complete Node/affected suites and explicit integration cases supply proof independent of local CI selection. V11 local mode reports only its actual selected scope; it must not be claimed as a full-branch run merely because it runs at M4. If a PR is later authorized, the plan expressly requires the actual full base/head PR-mode command. Applicable unchanged evidence can be reused only on affirmative exact-source/procedure/environment basis, with no freshly changed input covered by an old pass.

Command and completion assessment: inspected repository entrypoints and existing runner options; the 28 distinct directly named executable script/module entry paths checked all exist. V2/V4/V6 retain the specified harness entrypoints while adapting obsolete positive bodies, and additional affected complete modules are required by real imports. Unexpected command removal requires reviewed amendment, not skipping a check. Temporary output is task-owned, existing builders regenerate metadata, and historical release entries remain untouched. Manual evidence has explicit inspection scope and semantic questions; it complements runtime assertions rather than replaces them.

Final dependency: the plan separately names fresh independent final whole-change Code Review after all four milestones/corrections, followed by distinct Verify. Neither M4 review, green integrated tests nor a group non-applicability label can waive it. External push/PR/release authority remains separate. The owner-confirmed completion baseline is not recast as a runtime pass, and historical failed M4 audit/drift remains disclosed.

No material sequencing, allocation, retained-protection, boundary-proof or necessary-owner-decision finding emerged. The plan is adequate for authorized implementation in its stated slices. This review does not execute those slices, establish implementation correctness, final Verify or branch/PR readiness, and does not automatically hand off or initialize work. Authoring checks are reported structural/readability evidence only (current clarification reports89 readability warnings); no runtime tests were executed by this Delivery Review.
independence_basis: Separate delegated nonauthor agent /root/independent_proposal_review read the complete plan, current exact Design/proposal/concern basis and relevant implementation imports/commands. The author alone created the plan. Earlier independent upstream reviews are not plan authorship; this reviewer records only its own scoped judgment and applicability.
